phrases.text: So
welcome back again.
It's time to solve one more problem.
Now, in this problem,
we are given two trains.
The length of the first train is one hundred sixty meter,
and the length of the second train is one hundred forty meters.
Their speeds are fifty-four kilometers per hour
and thirty-six kilometers per hour.
Also, the question clearly says
both trains are moving in opposite directions.
The question is asking us to find in how many seconds they will completely cross each other.
Now, the important point here is
completely cross each other.
What does that mean?
It means both trains have to pass each other fully.
So together, they need to cover the sum of their lengths, not just one train's length.
The total distance will be one hundred sixty
plus one hundred forty,
which is three hundred meter. Got it?
Perfect.
Now, one more thing.
Since both trains are moving in opposite directions,
their speeds add up.
This is the basic concept. When two objects move towards each other,
the distance between them decreases using the relative speed, and for opposite directions, we simply add the speeds.
So the relative speed becomes fifty-four plus thirty-six, which is ninety kilometers per hour.

Now, we cannot use kilometers per hour because our distance is in meters, so let us convert it into meters per second. Ninety multiplied by five over eighteen gives us twenty-five meters per second. Now everything is ready. We know the total distance is three hundred meters, and the relative speed is twenty-five meters per second. So using the formula,
time equals distance divided by speed. Putting the values,
time equals three hundred divided by twenty-five. After solving this, we get twelve seconds. Hence, the trains will completely cross each other in twelve seconds. So the correct option is option B.
